facts.statement: Tenontosaurus had a long, broad tail and stiff back supported by a network of bony tendons.
facts.quote: It had an unusually long, broad tail, which like its back was stiffened with a network of bony tendons.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus lived in western North America between 115 and 108 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The genus is known from the late Aptian to Albian ages of the Early Cretaceous period sediments of western North America, dating between 115 and 108 million years ago.

facts.statement: The first fossil of Tenontosaurus was discovered in 1903 in Big Horn County, Montana, by an AMNH expedition.
facts.quote: The first Tenontosaurus fossil was found in Big Horn County, Montana by an American Museum of Natural History (AMNH) expedition in 1903.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown informally named the animal "Tenantosaurus" or "sinew lizard" due to its stiffening tendons.
facts.quote: Barnum Brown gave it the informal name "Tenantosaurus", "sinew lizard", in reference to the extensive system of stiffening tendons in its back and tail.

facts.statement: John Ostrom scientifically described the genus as Tenontosaurus tilletti in 1970 based on fossils from the Cloverly Formation.
facts.quote: Following his expedition, in 1970, Ostrom published a review of the fauna and geology of the Cloverly Formation. In that paper, he scientifically described Brown's taxon, calling it Tenontosaurus tilletti.

facts.statement: The species name tilletti honors the Lloyd Tillett family who assisted Yale expeditions.
facts.quote: The species name refers to the Lloyd Tillett family, who provided field parties from Yale with assistance and hospitality throughout their expeditions.

facts.statement: A second species, T. dossi, was described in 1997 from fossils found at the Doss Ranch site in Texas.
facts.quote: In 1997, remains from the Twin Mountains Formation of Texas were assigned to a new species of Tenontosaurus, T. dossi, named after the Doss Ranch site.

facts.statement: New Tenontosaurus fossils were unearthed in 2025 from the Yucca Formation in Texas.
facts.quote: In 2025, Tenontosaurus were unearthed from the Yucca Formation in Texas.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus was a medium-sized ornithopod weighing approximately 1000 kg.
facts.quote: Tenontosaurus was a medium-sized ornithopod, with both species weighing about 1000 kg.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated that T. dossi was 7 meters long and weighed 1000 kg.
facts.quote: Paul also estimated that T. dossi would have been 7 m long and weighed 1000 kg.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus possessed a thick, U-shaped beak formed by flaring premaxillae, a trait characteristic of iguanodontians.
facts.quote: The premaxillae flared inferiorly (towards the bottom), forming a thick, U-shaped beak, characteristic of iguanodontians.

facts.statement: The vomer was the longest bone in the Tenontosaurus skull, extending from the beak to the back of the eye socket.
facts.quote: The single longest bone in Tenontosaurus' skull is the vomer, which stretches from the middle of the beak to the very back of the orbital cavity (eye socket).

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Tenontosaurus ended in a predentary bone, a structure unique to ornithischians that formed the lower beak.
facts.quote: It terminated in a predentary bone, a structure found uniquely among ornithischians which formed the lower beak.

facts.statement: The horseshoe-shaped predentary of Tenontosaurus was lined with projecting serrations called pseudo-teeth or denticles.
facts.quote: The predentary in Tenontosaurus was horseshoe-shaped and was lined with projecting serrations, referred to as pseudo-teeth, or as denticles.

facts.statement: All teeth in Tenontosaurus were enameled on only one side, the inner or medial surface.
facts.quote: All of Tenontosaurus' teeth were enameled unilaterally (on only one side, that being medially, or on the inside).

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus was a facultative quadruped capable of standing on two or four legs.
facts.quote: Tenontosaurus was a facultative quadruped, capable of assuming either a bipedal or quadrupedal stance.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus likely used a quadrupedal stance for feeding but was probably unable to move rapidly on four legs.
facts.quote: It may have used a quadrupedal stance while feeding, but was probably incapable of rapid quadrupedal movement.

facts.statement: The front feet of Tenontosaurus displayed a mix of traits associated with both bipedal and quadrupedal locomotion.
facts.quote: The manus (the hand/front foot) shows a mixture of traits associated with bipeds and quadrupeds.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus is classified as a genus of iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Tenontosaurus ( ; ) is a genus of iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur.

facts.statement: The genus Tenontosaurus contains two species: T. tilletti and T. dossi.
facts.quote: It contains two species, Tenontosaurus tilletti (described by John Ostrom in 1970) and Tenontosaurus dossi (described by Winkler, Murry, and Jacobs in 1997).

facts.statement: It is debated whether Ostrom's original reconstruction of the Tenontosaurus skull accurately represented its true depth.
facts.quote: Ostrom's reconstruction of the skull exaggerated the overall depth of the skull, leading to one which more closely resembles that of Hypsilophodon.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus was originally placed in the family Iguanodontidae but later reclassified into Hypsilophodontidae.
facts.quote: Tenontosaurus was originally classified in the family Iguanodontidae, although subsequent authors challenged this classification and proposed it actually belonged to Hypsilophodontidae.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic studies describe Tenontosaurus as an intermediate non-dryomorph iguanodont between Hypsilophodon-like and Iguanodon-like groups.
facts.quote: Subsequent phylogenetic analyses have found Tenontosaurus to be intermediate in position between Hypsilophodon-like taxa and Iguanodon-like taxa, as a non-dryomorph iguanodont.

facts.statement: As a low browser, an adult Tenontosaurus could reach a maximum height of about 3 meters when standing bipedally.
facts.quote: Tenontosaurus was a low browser, and an adult would have had a maximum browsing height of about 3 m if it adopted a bipedal stance.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus possessed a powerful U-shaped beak and angled teeth that allowed it to consume leaves, wood, and fruit.
facts.quote: Its powerful, U-shaped beak and the angled cutting surfaces of its teeth, however, meant it was not limited to which part of the plant it consumed.

facts.statement: Fossil teeth and skeletons of the theropod Deinonychus are frequently found associated with Tenontosaurus tilletti remains.
facts.quote: Teeth and a number of skeletons belonging to the carnivorous theropod Deinonychus have often been discovered associated with Tenontosaurus tilletti remains.

facts.statement: Approximately 20% of Tenontosaurus fossils are found near Deinonychus, leading some scientists to suggest Deinonychus was its major predator.
facts.quote: In all, 20% of Tenontosaurus fossils are found in close proximity to Deinonychus, and several scientists have suggested that this implies Deinonychus was the major predator of Tenontosaurus.

facts.statement: Medullary bone tissue found in a Tenontosaurus specimen indicates it used this tissue for reproduction, a trait also seen in egg-laying birds.
facts.quote: The presence of medullary bone tissue in the thigh bone and shin bone of one specimen indicates that Tenontosaurus used this tissue, today only found in birds that are laying eggs, in reproduction.

facts.statement: The presence of medullary bone in Tenontosaurus suggests that early-diverging dinosaur lineages reached reproductive maturity before achieving maximum size.
facts.quote: Because the theropod line of dinosaurs that includes Allosaurus and Tyrannosaurus diverged from the line that led to Tenontosaurus very early in the evolution of dinosaurs, this suggests that dinosaurs in general produced medullary tissue and reached reproductive maturity before maximum size.

facts.statement: Histological analysis reveals Tenontosaurus grew rapidly as a juvenile and sub-adult but slowed significantly near maturity, unlike other iguanodontians.
facts.quote: A histological study showed that T. tilletti grew quickly early in life and during sub-adult ontogeny, but grew very slowly in the years approaching maturity, unlike other iguanodontians.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus lived in a paleoenvironment of tropical or sub-tropical forests, floodplains, and swamps similar to modern-day Louisiana.
facts.quote: The paleoenvironment of the Antlers Formation consisted of tropical or sub-tropical forests, floodplains, river deltas, coastal swamps, bayous and lagoons, probably similar to that of modern-day Louisiana.

facts.statement: In the Cloverly Formation, Tenontosaurus was the most abundant vertebrate, five times more common than the next most frequent species, Sauropelta.
facts.quote: Throughout the Cloverly Formation, Tenontosaurus is by far the most common vertebrate, five times more abundant than the next most common, the ankylosaur Sauropelta.

facts.statement: In the arid Little Sheep Mudstone Member, Tenontosaurus was the sole herbivorous dinosaur, sharing its habitat with Deinonychus, an allosauroid theropod, and a goniopholid crocodile.
facts.quote: In the arid Little Sheep Mudstone Member, Tenontosaurus is the only herbivorous dinosaur, and it shared its environment with the common predator Deinonychus as well as an indeterminate species of allosauroid theropod and goniopholid crocodile.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus lived during the middle Cretaceous period, between approximately 122 and 108 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivieron a mediados del período Cretácico, entre aproximadamente 122 a 108 millones de años desde el Aptiense al Albiense

facts.statement: Fossils of Tenontosaurus have been found in what is now North America.
facts.quote: en lo que es hoy Norteamérica

facts.statement: When Tenontosaurus first appeared in Wyoming and Montana, the climate was arid to semi-arid with seasonal rainfall and occasional droughts.
facts.quote: At the time Tenontosaurus first appeared in Wyoming and Montana (the early Albian age), the regions climate was arid to semi-arid, dry, with seasonal periods of rainfall and occasional droughts.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus populations increased in abundance during a dramatic shift from arid to wetter climates, showing it was a remarkably adaptable animal.
facts.quote: This dramatic shift in climate coincided with an apparent increase, rather than decrease, in the abundance of Tenontosaurus.

facts.statement: The genus Tenontosaurus was named by John Ostrom in 1970.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Ostrom, 1970

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Tenontosaurus tilletti.
facts.quote: type_species: Tenontosaurus tilletti

facts.statement: A second species, Tenontosaurus dossi, was described by Winkler, Murray, and Jacobs in 1997.
facts.quote: subdivision: Tenontosaurus dossi Winkler, Murray & Jacobs, 1997

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus measured between 6.5 and 8 meters in length, stood 2.2 meters tall, and weighed between 1 and 2 tons.
facts.quote: Los tenontosaurios median entre 6,5 y 8 metros de longitud, 2,2 de altura y pesaba de 1 a 2 toneladas.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus had long forelimbs with hands equipped with five stout fingers.
facts.quote: Presentaban extremidades delanteras largas con manos provistas de cinco rollizos dedos

facts.statement: The head ended in a beak with cheek teeth aligned on the sides.
facts.quote: Su cabeza terminaba en pico con muelas alineadas a los lados

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus had long legs with feet equipped with four stout toes.
facts.quote: sus piernas eran largas con patas provistas de cuatro rollizos dedos

facts.statement: Its back was rigid with a network of bony tendons, which likely forced it to walk on all fours for long periods.
facts.quote: su espalda estaba rígida con una red de tendones óseos, cosa que lo habría obligado a andar mucho tiempo en cuatro patas

facts.statement: Length is not a good indicator of weight in Tenontosaurus because its tail is very long.
facts.quote: La longitud no es una buena indicación del peso en Tenontosaurus porque la cola es muy larga.

facts.statement: The skull of Tenontosaurus was low and long, appearing very elongated when viewed from above.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Tenontosaurus es bajo y largo, muy alargado cuando se ve desde arriba

facts.statement: There was a huge oval nasal fossa sloping backward in the curve of the snout.
facts.quote: En la curva del hocico hay una enorme fosa nasal ovalada inclinada hacia atrás

facts.statement: The premaxillae together formed a bony core of the upper beak that hung below the jaw edge.
facts.quote: Los premaxilares juntos forman un núcleo óseo del pico superior que cuelga por debajo del borde de la mandíbula.

facts.statement: The true dentary teeth of the lower jaw had a prominent vertical main ridge.
facts.quote: Los dientes dentarios verdaderos de la mandíbula inferior tienen una cresta principal vertical prominente.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus had a spine consisting of twelve cervical vertebrae, fifteen dorsal vertebrae, six sacral vertebrae, and at least sixty-one tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: La columna vertebral consta de doce vértebras cervicales, quince vértebras dorsales, seis vértebras sacras y al menos sesenta y una vértebras de la cola.

facts.statement: The tail of Tenontosaurus was very long, making up at least 57% of the animal's total length, and in some cases up to two-thirds.
facts.quote: La cola es muy larga y constituye al menos el 57% de la longitud del animal, en algunos casos hasta dos tercios.

facts.statement: The spine of Tenontosaurus was rigid due to ossified tendons running along the back, sacrum, and anterior and middle parts of the tail.
facts.quote: La columna vertebral está rígida por tendones osificados que recorren la espalda, el sacro y la cola anterior y media.

facts.statement: The spinous processes of the sacral vertebrae were even longer and tilted significantly backward.
facts.quote: Las apófisis espinosas de las vértebras sacras son aún más largas y se inclinan bastante hacia atrás.

facts.statement: The chevrons in the middle of the tail were nearly vertical and gradually widened toward their lower ends.
facts.quote: Los cheurones aquí, teniendo en cuenta la curvatura de la cola, son casi verticales y se ensanchan gradualmente hacia sus extremos inferiores.

facts.statement: Ossified tendons running along the spinous processes and chevrons likely made the tail a rigid structure to support huge retractor muscles that pulled the femurs backward during walking.
facts.quote: Los tendones osificados recorren las apófisis espinosas y los cheurones hasta llegar a este extremo, lo que debe haber convertido a la cola en una estructura muy rígida, presumiblemente para soportar los enormes músculos retractores que tiraban de los fémures hacia atrás al caminar.

facts.statement: The scapula of Tenontosaurus had a straight leading edge and a much more curved trailing edge.
facts.quote: El escapula tiene un borde de ataque recto y un borde de salida mucho más curvo.

facts.statement: The coracoid had a powerful posterior tip and was perforated by a coracoid foramen that did not touch the bony suture with the scapula.
facts.quote: El coracoides tiene una poderosa punta posterior y está perforado por un foramen coracoideo que no toca la costura ósea con la escápula.

facts.statement: Large crescent-shaped ossified sternums have been found in several Tenontosaurus specimens.
facts.quote: Se han encontrado grandes esternones osificados en forma de media luna en varios especímenes.

facts.statement: The forelimb of Tenontosaurus was long and robust, reaching approximately 68% of the hindlimb's length.
facts.quote: La extremidad anterior es larga y robusta en aproximadamente el 68% de la longitud de la extremidad posterior.

facts.statement: The robust humerus had a fairly low but powerful deltopectoral crest.
facts.quote: El húmero robusto tiene una cresta deltopectoral bastante baja pero poderosa.

facts.statement: The hand was short and wide with five fingers, where the width was one and a half times the length.
facts.quote: La mano es corta y ancha con cinco dedos. El ancho es una vez y media el largo.

facts.statement: The thumb had an enlarged first phalanx and was positioned to the side but did not bear a large claw.
facts.quote: El pulgar tiene una primera falange ensanchada y está de lado pero no lleva una garra grande.

facts.statement: The phalanx formula was 2-3-3-2-2 or 2-3-3-1-1, meaning the third finger had three phalanges instead of four, as its ancestors had.
facts.quote: La fórmula de las falanges es 2-3-3-2-2 o 2-3-3-1-1. Por lo tanto, el tercer dedo tiene tres falanges en lugar de cuatro, como todavía tenían los ancestros de Tenontosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2013, Jonathan Tennant described the postcranial skeleton using specimen LL.12275.
facts.quote: En 2013, Jonathan Tennant describió el esqueleto poscraneal utilizando el espécimen LL.12275.

facts.statement: In 2015, the skull was described in detail using a new specimen, OMNH 58340, which was found in 2000.
facts.quote: En 2015, el cráneo se describió con gran detalle utilizando un nuevo espécimen, OMNH 58340, encontrado en 2000.

facts.statement: Although Tenontosaurus's light structure resembles a hypsilophodontid, detailed examination suggests it is likely a basal member of Iguanodontia.
facts.quote: La estructura ligera de Tenontosaurus recuerda a un hipsilofodonte, pero un examen más detallado ha revelado que es muy probable que sea un miembro basal de Iguanodontia.

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus lived from the Aptian to the Cenomanian stages, between 121.4 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Cenomanian (121.4 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Tenontosaurus was a low browser, and an adult would have had a maximum feeding height of about 3 meters if it adopted a bipedal posture.
facts.quote: Tenontosaurus era un ramoneador bajo, y un adulto habría tenido una altura máxima de alimentación de unos 3 metros si adoptara una postura bípeda.

facts.statement: Leaves, wood, and even fruit may have formed part of Tenontosaurus's diet.
facts.quote: Las hojas, la madera e incluso la fruta pudieron haber formado parte de su dieta.

facts.statement: The presence of medullary bone in the femur and tibia of a specimen indicates that Tenontosaurus used this tissue, found today only in egg-laying birds, for reproduction.
facts.quote: La presencia de tejido óseo medular en el fémur y la tibia de un espécimen indica que los tenontosaurios usaron este tejido, que hoy solo se encuentra en aves que están poniendo huevos, en la reproducción.

facts.statement: A histological study showed that T. tilletti grew rapidly during its early years and sub-adult stage, then slowed its growth rate as it approached maturity, unlike other iguanodonts.
facts.quote: Un estudio histológico mostró que T. tilletti creció rápidamente durante sus primeros años de vida y en su etapa de sub-adulto, tras lo cual ralentizava su ritmo de crecimiento en los años que se aproximaban a la madurez, a diferencia de otros iguanodontes.

facts.statement: Like Tyrannosaurus and Allosaurus, this individual Tenontosaurus did not reach full adult size before dying at 8 years old.
facts.quote: al igual que Tyrannosaurus y Allosaurus, otros dos dinosaurios que se sabe que produjeron hueso medular, el individuo no alcanzó el tamaño adulto completo tras su muerte a los 8 años.

facts.statement: The position of Tenontosaurus in the evolutionary tree was very problematic and controversial due to a lack of adequate cladistic analysis.
facts.quote: La posición de Tenontosaurus en el árbol genealógico evolutivo fue muy problemática y controvertida. Faltaba un análisis cladístico adecuado.
